subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should session-memory sync move to a persisted append-only incremental index for JSONL transcripts, or should OpenClaw treat the current cache/batch plus full dirty-file rebuild as the intended boundary for now?
rationale: The source-reproducible problem is real, but the permanent fix affects SQLite metadata, chunk overlap semantics, compaction behavior, and session-state freshness; automation should not choose that product/storage contract while the related PR is conflicting and proof-labeled.

options.title: Sponsor incremental indexing
options.body: Define a persisted high-water-mark or chunk manifest design that handles overlap and compaction fallback, then update or replace the related pull request with focused tests and live proof.

options.title: Keep cache and batch behavior
options.body: Accept the current full dirty-file rebuild as the supported implementation and narrow this issue to docs or performance tuning only.

options.title: Fold into archival policy
options.body: Defer per-file incrementality and track the remaining work through a broader session retention, rotation, and compaction design.

recommendation.title: Sponsor incremental indexing
recommendation.body: Define a persisted high-water-mark or chunk manifest design that handles overlap and compaction fallback, then update or replace the related pull request with focused tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent session sync helper extraction is the closest maintainer-routing signal for the dirty-session planning layer.
